items.claim: The row holds all fifteen verses as one row on the stated ground that a single addressee in second-masculine-singular address governs the full span of MT 35:1-35:15, and that ground is untrue at two verses: MT 35:9 carries a second-masculine-plural verb of knowing, and MT 35:13 carries three second-masculine-plural forms and no second-masculine-singular form at all. The same premise is what the row uses to decline the internal splits at MT 35:4/35:5 and at MT 35:9/35:10, so the premise, not the span, is what needs correcting. The row already discloses the plural form at MT 35:9 in one field while asserting uniform singular address in two others.
items.both_sides: Front seam: a petuchah stands after MT 34:31 and MT 35:1 carries the strict-form onset formula, so the onset side is firm. Close seam: MT 35:15 ends with the third-person-plural recognition refrain and a petuchah follows it. Interior: the single interior paragraph mark is the setumah after MT 35:13, and it coincides with neither proposed internal split. The witness therefore supports the boundary exactly where the row puts it; only the uniform-address claim fails.

suggested_fix.fact: the address inside the oracle alternates: second-masculine-plural at MT 35:9 and MT 35:13, second-masculine-singular elsewhere in the chapter

items.claim: Every Hebrew and paragraph fact this row asserts over MT 36:1-36:12 holds on the bytes, including the count that is most exposed to correction: MT 36:2-36:7 carries six messenger formulas, one in each of the six verses, and no recognition or utterance refrain stands between any two of them, so the row's six and its non-cutting reading are both byte-true. A seven-count for the same stretch is accounted for by MT 36:4, which carries a summons to hear the word of the Lord YHWH before its messenger formula; that is a second speech-introduction of a different kind, not a seventh messenger formula.
items.both_sides: Front seam: the petuchah after MT 35:15 and the son-of-man sub-onset at MT 36:1. Close seam: the second-masculine-plural knowing refrain at MT 36:11, the inheritance restatement at MT 36:12 and a setumah after MT 36:12, with the addressee turning to feminine singular in the next verse. Both sides carry evidence independent of the other.

items.claim: Two stated facts on this row are untrue as written. First, at MT 36:16 the row calls its onset the fourth and last hard seam of its kind since MT 33:1 and enumerates MT 33:1, MT 33:23 and MT 34:1; the same onset form also stands at MT 35:1, which makes MT 36:16 the fifth in that enumeration, and it is not the last, because the identical form stands again at MT 37:15 and at MT 38:1. Second, the translation quotation the row attaches to MT 36:22 is not verbatim: it is written with a straight apostrophe where the translation carries a right single quotation mark.
items.both_sides: Onset side is the strongest class available: a setumah after MT 36:15 and the strict-form onset formula at MT 36:16, byte-identical to the form at MT 35:1. Close side is the weaker one and is the same seam challenged on the following row: MT 36:23 does carry the utterance formula and a recognition clause naming the nations, but the utterance formula is not verse-final and no paragraph mark stands after MT 36:23.

suggested_fix.fact: the onsets of this form from MT 33:1 onward stand at MT 33:1, MT 33:23, MT 34:1, MT 35:1, MT 36:16, MT 37:15 and MT 38:1, so MT 36:16 is the fifth of them and not the last

items.claim: The row opens on a sub-onset it calls 'for' at MT 36:24, and MT 36:24 carries no causal or explanatory particle: it opens with waw plus a first-person perfect, the same construction that carries on through MT 36:25-36:28. The 'For' belongs to the translation, which supplies it and also prints a paragraph there, and translation formatting cannot carry a boundary. On the witness this front seam has neither an onset device nor a paragraph mark: the nearest marks fall after MT 36:21 and after MT 36:32, so the closed section runs MT 36:22-36:32 and this row's opening lies inside it.
items.both_sides: Onset side, MT 36:23/36:24: the close at MT 36:23 is genuine, the utterance formula plus a recognition clause naming the nations, but that formula is not verse-final, no paragraph mark follows MT 36:23, and MT 36:24 supplies no onset device of its own. Close side, MT 36:32/36:33: firm, the utterance formula at MT 36:32 with a setumah after it and a messenger re-onset at MT 36:33. Inside MT 36:16-36:38 the only devices that re-open a speech are the messenger formulas at MT 36:22, MT 36:33 and MT 36:37; none stands at MT 36:24. The row is well-founded at its close and under-supported at its onset, so the grade rather than the span is what should move.

items.claim: At MT 36:36 the row names only the emphatic closing clause, and the verse carries more than that: before the emphatic clause it carries a third-person-plural recognition clause that names the nations, the same construction disclosed at MT 36:23. The internal close the row is grading as non-final therefore stacks a recognition clause, an emphatic clause and a setumah, which is the same combination the row treats as row-final at MT 36:38, and that is precisely the comparison the row's internal-versus-final decision turns on.
items.both_sides: Non-finality at MT 36:36 is nonetheless correctly grounded: a messenger re-onset follows at MT 36:37, so the row cannot end at MT 36:36. Front seam: the utterance formula at MT 36:32 with a setumah after it, and a messenger re-onset at MT 36:33. Close seam: the third-person-plural recognition refrain at MT 36:38 with a setumah after it, and the hand-of-YHWH vision onset in the next verse. The span stands; the disclosure at MT 36:36 is what is short.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: Instances for the already-routed read-form question, recorded and not adjudicated. Seven read forms are rendered across this cluster: one at MT 35:9, one at MT 35:12, two at MT 36:13, two at MT 36:14 and one at MT 36:15. None of the seven occurs anywhere in the running-text extract, which carries the written forms at those sites; each reconstructs its witness note entry exactly, codepoint for codepoint, once the morpheme separator is removed; and three of the seven entries carry a separator in the witness while four carry none. I reproduce none of the seven here and name the sites instead.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: the pending decision governs seven renderings in this cluster alone, and the two sub-cases are not the same question: a separator removed from an entry that has one is a rendering choice, while an entry that never had one cannot have been stripped, which is the narrower point my MT 35:9, MT 35:12, MT 36:13 and MT 36:14 findings rest on

unresolved_uncertainty.what: Whether a row must disclose a non-variant editorial note carried by a verse inside its span. The witness carries such a note on MT 36:7, recording an accent read differently from the printed edition, and the row covering MT 36:1-36:12 cites MT 36:7 as evidence without disclosing the note. The note layer is described as single-witness apparatus to be disclosed, but the corpus is not uniform: of the thirty-six rows whose spans cover such a note, twenty-six disclose it and ten do not. I did not score this against the row, because the expectation is not settled and the device the row cites at that verse does not turn on accents.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: it decides whether a low finding stands on that row and on the nine others that are silent, and it is cheaper to rule once than to re-litigate per row

unresolved_uncertainty.what: The reference-mirror flags on five of my rows are answered as legitimate, with one exception I did not score. On four of them the unmirrored references are produced by prose that names a larger span or a comparison site, each labelled as comparison or as a shared frame, and none is offered as that row's own boundary evidence. The exception is the row covering MT 36:24-36:32, whose boundary evidence list includes MT 11:19: that reference is a lexical contrast twenty-five chapters away and bears on neither of the row's two seams, and the flag did not catch it.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: whether a cross-chapter lexical contrast may sit in a boundary-evidence field is a filing convention rather than a fact about the text, so it is not mine to decide; but the mirror check evidently does not see it, which is worth knowing before the check is relied on as complete
